label: early original-phase inputs of q/g/y/l/3/a (q strongest)
explanation: Mostly a token-and-position unit. About 74% of activation mass falls in the original phase, peaking at t=1-3 and falling off after t=4. It is driven by the current input: q gives the most (rate 0.40, 39% of mass), then g, y, l, 3 and a. Strongest on q at t=1-2 when the token before is q or 3 (top examples: q q q, 3 q q, q 3 q). q at t<=3 in the original phase is active 87% of the time. A second, weaker component (about 25% of mass) appears late in the copy phase (recall_idx >= 3, rate rising with recall_idx) with no clear token identity. It is nearly silent at the delimiter and the first copy steps (recall_idx 0-2), and almost never fires on q during the copy phase. The firing set depends on context, so token identity plus position gets only about 0.34 precision and 0.51 recall.
